title: In situ structure of the poxvirus portal complex.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) search API: 3 portal-complex maps released 2026-07-22 (EMD-53128 in mature virions, EMD-55456 in cytoplasmic cores, EMD-55457 in isolated cores), plus 2 earlier entries from 2024 (EMD-18916 tomogram, EMD-18917 average). Queried RCSB PDB: one atomic model, 9QG7, with 5 polymer entities at 8.21 Å resolution. I did not download the map files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paywalled, no PMCID): cryo-ET (cryo-electron tomography) with subtomogram averaging of a hexameric E8/E6/L3 portal, and D5 helicase docking. No supplement or data statement could be retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: EMDB maps and PDB 9QG7 are public and open; I confirmed the entries exist through the APIs but didn't download the maps.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The deposits are 3D density maps and a single structural model. There is no table of examples with an outcome column, so any label would have to be built from scratch.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are maps and one coordinate model, not a feature table of many items.

a4_units_stated.note: Map voxel sizes and resolution (8.21 Å for 9QG7) are standard EMDB/PDB metadata.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 5 maps and 1 model (5 protein chains) in total, far below the ~400-row minimum. Subtomogram particle counts aren't labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; the maps are probably hundreds of MB, and the raw tomograms (EMPIAR) are much larger
a6_fits_laptop.note: I didn't check this; it doesn't matter given the A2/A5 failures.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: There is no count to reconcile: the 3 new maps match the 3 conditions described in the abstract (mature virions, cytoplasmic cores, isolated cores).

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable, since there is no label. The model was partly built with structure prediction, so any per-residue label taken from it would be partly a model's output.

honest_claim_h3: None possible: a single structure of one complex gives no set of labelled examples to learn from.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the 3D shape of the poxvirus core pore to predict which viral proteins bind it or which drugs could block it.
plain_idea.train_on: About 5 electron-density maps and 1 atomic model of a single protein complex; the number of labelled examples is effectively zero.
plain_idea.predict: There is no measured outcome to predict; any target, such as binding sites or druggability, would have to be invented or taken from other models.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Structural biologists and antiviral drug designers care about the portal, but this deposit is a structure to use as a reference, not a training set.

ml_idea: None viable. At most, use 9QG7 as a single test case, for example checking whether AlphaFold-Multimer predicts the E6/E8/L3 assembly, but that is a one-structure comparison, not an ML project.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the project fails Part A on the number of examples.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited entries: 3 new EMDB maps plus 1 PDB model (already done; this check kills the project).

verdict_reason: A single cryo-ET structure deposit (3 new EMDB maps plus PDB 9QG7, 5 protein chains at 8.2 Å) has no label column and only about 5 items, so it fails A2 and A5.
